rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.
Processing user-controlled object hierarchies inefficiently can lead to denial of service.
An attempt to use a value that is not an object or 'null' as a prototype will either be ignored or result in a runtime error.
DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.
Transforming hard-coded data (such as hexadecimal constants) into code to be executed is a technique often associated with backdoors and should be avoided.
An expression that has no effect and is used in a void context is most likely redundant and may indicate a bug.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Including functionality from an untrusted source may allow an attacker to control the functionality and execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.
An expression that has no effect and is used in a void context is most likely redundant and may indicate a bug.
Processing user-controlled object hierarchies inefficiently can lead to denial of service.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.
Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
rules.description: Creating a temporary file that is accessible by other users can lead to information disclosure and sometimes remote code execution.
DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.
